record.paper_title: Four nucleon systems: a zoom to the open problems in nuclear interaction
record.context_brief: Placement of the first excited helium-4 0+ resonance
record.original_question: How can a nuclear interaction model simultaneously reproduce the alpha-particle ground state, the triton threshold, and the position and width of the first excited helium-4 state with spin-parity 0+ that controls very-low-energy proton plus tritium scattering below the neutron plus helium-3 threshold? The model must treat the Coulomb separation of the proton plus tritium and neutron plus helium-3 thresholds properly, because the low-energy excitation function and singlet scattering length are highly sensitive to whether the 0+ resonance is placed correctly relative to those thresholds.

evidence.quote: Separation of n+3He and p+3H channels requires proper treatment of Coulomb interaction, the task is furthermore burden since both thresholds are described by the same isospin quantum numbers.

In order to reproduce the shape of experimental excitation function, NN interaction model is obliged with high accurately situate 4He excited state. In fact, width of the resonance is strongly correlated with its relative position to p+3H threshold.

As have been shown, description of low energy p+3H completely relies on success in reproducing position and width of the first excited state of α-particle. However position of this resonant state seems to be strongly correlated with position of predicted triton threshold and α-particle ground state.

artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work using ab initio methods (no-core Gamow shell model, hyperspherical harmonics with chiral NN+3N interactions) has made significant progress in describing the 0₂⁺ proton-decaying resonance of ⁴He and p+³H low-energy scattering, with calculations reproducing the resonance energy and width and the monopole form factor reasonably well. However, simultaneous quantitative reproduction of the ⁴He ground state, the ³H threshold, and the precise position/width of the 0⁺ resonance remains sensitive to the choice of NN+3N interaction and regulator cutoff, so the problem is partially resolved rather than fully solved.

status_evidence.title: Description of the Proton-Decaying 0₂⁺ Resonance of the α Particle
status_evidence.snippet: Coupled-channel no-core Gamow shell model with [3H+p], [3He+n], [2H+2H] channels explains excitation energy and monopole form factor of the 0+ state.
status_evidence.claim: Recent ab initio frameworks describe the 0₂⁺ resonance, indicating partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Nuclear Resonances, Scattering and Reactions from First Principles
status_evidence.snippet: In p+3H scattering below the n+3He channel, 3N forces are appreciable and show clear cutoff dependence.
status_evidence.claim: Reproduction of low-energy p+³H observables depends sensitively on the 3N interaction and regulator, so simultaneous fits are not yet definitive.

status_evidence.title: Study of the alpha-particle monopole transition form factor
status_evidence.snippet: Modern chiral NN+3N calculations of the 4He 0+ resonance and monopole transition.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing efforts continue to refine the description, consistent with partial resolution.
